notes: Behavioral evals for the prototype skill. Each targets a place a generic agent would default the wrong way: reskinning instead of genuinely varying, taking on a page-sized ask without narrowing it, ignoring a requested variation count, or carrying prototype shortcuts into the real build. Run a fresh agent that reads SKILL.md (not the evals) per prompt, then grade the output against the expectations.

evals.name: basic-five-variations
evals.prompt: Prototype the empty state for our dashboard — what should it look like when there's no data yet?
evals.expected_output: Generates 5 genuinely different interactive variations of the empty state in one self-contained HTML file, each named with a one-line tradeoff note, saved to prototypes/ and opened.
expectations: Produces 5 variations by default (unless the user asked for a different count)
Each variation reflects a genuinely different interaction/layout approach, not a recolor of the same idea
Output is a single self-contained HTML file — vanilla HTML/CSS/JS, no build step, no CDN, no framework
Each variation has a short name and a one-line tradeoff note
Variations share the same fake content/data for a fair comparison
File is saved under prototypes/<feature-name>.html and opened

evals.name: page-sized-ask-scopes-down
evals.prompt: Prototype our new settings screen — I want to see a few different directions for the whole thing.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes the ask is page-sized rather than one feature, and asks which specific piece to prototype first instead of attempting to mock up the whole screen in variations.
expectations: Does not immediately generate 5 full-screen variations
Asks which single feature/piece of the settings screen to prototype first
Briefly explains that prototyping works best on one feature at a time

evals.name: custom-count-honored
evals.prompt: Mock up 3 different takes on our notification toast — keep it quick.
evals.expected_output: Honors the requested count of 3 variations instead of defaulting to 5, while keeping each one genuinely distinct.
expectations: Produces exactly 3 variations, not the default 5
Each of the 3 is still a genuinely different approach, not filler
Still follows the one self-contained HTML file format

evals.name: post-selection-real-build
evals.prompt: I looked at the 5 grid-density prototypes you made and I want to go with variation 3, the stepped notches one. Build that for real.
evals.expected_output: Builds variation 3 for real in the actual project using the project's real CSS architecture and real data/state, rather than copying the throwaway prototype file's inline styles or fake data into the codebase.
expectations: Builds the chosen variation as a real component in the project, not by copying the prototype file's markup wholesale
Uses the project's actual CSS architecture (e.g. @layer config, reset, elements, components) instead of the prototype's inline styles
Wires the component to real state/data rather than the prototype's fake data
Leaves the original prototype file in place as a record unless told to delete it
